mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, or GDP growth decelerates in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or INDPRO rebounds within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment, measured by the UNRATE series, signals a weakening labor market and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE declines within the next 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, S&P 500 returns tend to be negative over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS falls below 4% within 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both decline by more than 2% in a month, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will drag down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Either HOUST or RSAFS rebounds by > 2% within 2 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: If industrial production (INDPRO) grows by more than 2% in a quarter while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it indicates a supply-constrained economy that will experience inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 5% within 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI growth slows to < 0.2% per month within 3 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: If payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines by more than 100,000 jobs in a month while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is already above 6%, it signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will lead to a recession and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rebounds by > 100,000 jobs within 2 months, or SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances.
